title: Derived scalar tensor computes the finite continuous Koszul model
statement: Let E and Omega be normed fields in one universe, with a continuous E-algebra inclusion h. Let p,ell,r be natural numbers. Take the exact scalar restriction, action abelianness and ordinary derived invariant contexts of [lem-sfb-tame-inertia-continuous-koszul], and a normalized all-continuous E-coefficient realization dE for its admissible representations M. There exists a unit-normalized universal total left derived scalar tensor s [def-sfb-tame-inertia-scalar-mate-data] such that its comparison at the homotopy image of dE.koszul(M) is invertible for every M. This asserts existence and computation of derived scalar tensor; it asserts neither invertibility of a coefficient adjunct nor any comparison with derived Omega-invariants.

proof.text: Choose a basis of the finite-dimensional fixed subspace N. Continuous sections of the scalar-extended space identify with the finite product of coefficient rings. Subset coordinates identify every Koszul term with a finite free module, including zero rank.

Transport internal modules to sectionwise module sheaves. Finite free modules are flat, since tensoring with them is a finite direct sum. The complex vanishes outside [0,r], so apply the bounded-above flat K-flat theorem.

Transport the existing universal derived change-of-rings pair and its normalized adjunction back to internal modules. Adjoint uniqueness identifies ordinary tensor and its actual unit. The canonical comparison is invertible on the K-flat Koszul representatives. The normalized unit identity on all homotopy objects is the derived adjunction fraction formula with identity denominators.
